\title{Maximal universal invariants from quantum traces on finite quotients of Verma modules}
\author{Cristina Ana-Maria Anghel \and Jun Murakami}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\noindent\textbf{Source:} \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19113}{arXiv:2606.19113} \quad \textbf{Field:} math.GT\\

\section*{TL;DR}
The paper introduces a family of level-N universal quantum knot invariants constructed via quantum traces on finite-dimensional quotients of the Verma module of U\_q(sl\_2), valued in two-variable polynomial quotient rings. The novelty specialist rates the contribution significant (score 0.85, confidence 0.90): the construction is genuinely new, the prior-art landscape is correctly charted, and no missing prior art was identified. The technical-correctness specialist (overall: mostly\_sound, confidence 0.62) finds the braid-representation foundation (Theorem 4, C1) and the prime-N corollary (Corollary 9, C6) fully supported, but flags two major gaps: (1) the converse direction of the headline maximality claim in Theorem 8 is not explicitly proved --- the argument that any knot-invariant quotient must annihilate every generator of C\_N is missing, leaving open the possibility of cancellations in braid closures that the paper does not exclude (C4, major); (2) the 'richer structure' assertion for composite N in Remark 11 is entirely unsupported by computation --- no example knot pair is exhibited (C7, major). The interpolation formula proof (Theorem 39, C5) and the quantum-trace uniqueness proof (Theorem 29, C3) each contain typographic errors that impede independent verification, though the underlying arguments appear directionally correct. Lemma 31's inductive step is asserted without proof (C9, minor). The reproducibility specialist (score 0.22, confidence 0.86) flags the complete absence of computational or formal-proof artifacts as critical: no code repository, no worked examples, and no machine-checkable verification of the maximality theorem, in a field where computer-algebra verification of quantum invariants is standard. The citation specialist (confidence 1.00) finds the bibliography largely sound, with only minor clerical issues: a surname typo in [ADO] (Akustu for Akutsu) and self-citations [Cr1, Cr2] attributed to 'the second author' when C. Anghel is the first author of both. Because the paper is in a code-amenable field (math.QA/math.GT) and both reproducibility and technical-correctness flag missing proof artifacts for the headline maximality claim at critical and major severity respectively, the recommendation gate mandates major\_revision. The theoretical contribution is real and the mathematical gaps are addressable, but the converse of Theorem 8 requires a rigorous proof, Remark 11 needs either a computational example or downgrade to conjecture, the interpolation formula proof must be rewritten cleanly, and minimal computational verification artifacts must accompany the revision.

\textbf{Recommendation:} Major revision \quad \textbf{Confidence:} 74\%\\

\section*{Strengths}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item The construction of level-N universal quantum knot invariants over two-variable polynomial quotient rings is novel and cleanly separated from prior work on coloured Jones and ADO polynomials, which are defined only at roots of unity or at generic q but not simultaneously (novelty specialist, score 0.85).
  \item The braid-group representation result (Theorem 4 / Proposition 26) is fully supported: the R-matrix action on tensor powers of V\_N is shown to close in the quotient module modulo C\_N by explicit coefficient analysis (C1, technical\_correctness).
  \item The prime-N specialization (Corollary 9 / 35) is a clean consequence of the ideal-coincidence structure and is correctly derived once Theorem 8 is accepted, providing a concrete maximality statement for an infinite family of levels (C6, technical\_correctness).
  \item The algebraic framework --- quantum group U\_q(sl\_2) with divided powers, Verma module truncation, and two-variable quotient ring --- is well-motivated and correctly positioned relative to the Jackson-Kerler representation theory on which it builds (novelty specialist, relation: builds\_on).
  \item Citation hygiene is strong: the bibliography covers foundational texts on ADO invariants, the Volume Conjecture, non-semisimple TQFTs, and the Gukov-Manolescu conjecture, with no missing prior art identified by the novelty specialist.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Weaknesses}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item Theorem 8 / Theorem 34: the converse direction of the maximality claim is not proved --- the paper does not show that every generator of C\_N must vanish in any quotient ring yielding a knot invariant, leaving open the possibility that braid-closure cancellations could produce an invariant in a strictly larger quotient (C4, major, technical\_correctness).
  \item Remark 11 (richer structure for composite N) is completely unsupported: the claim that tilde \ensuremath{\Omega}\_N encodes information beyond the sequence (J\_d, \ensuremath{\Phi}\_d : d|N) is argued only heuristically via ideal structure, with no example knot pair distinguishing the universal invariant from the classical sequence (C7, major, technical\_correctness).
  \item The proof of Theorem 39 (interpolation formula) contains multiple typographic errors --- 's \ensuremath{-} 1\^{}\{1\ensuremath{-}N\}' for 's \ensuremath{-} q\^{}\{1\ensuremath{-}N\}', '\ensuremath{\phi}\_N(q)' for '\ensuremath{\phi}\_N(q\^{}2)', and a garbled factorization in the inductive step --- preventing mechanical independent verification of the paper's central identity (C5, major, technical\_correctness).
  \item No computational or formal-proof artifacts are provided in a code-amenable field: there is no code repository, no worked example computing \ensuremath{\Omega}\_N for any knot and level, and no machine-checkable verification of the headline maximality theorem, the ideal equalities, or the interpolation formula (C10, major / reproducibility critical).
  \item Lemma 31, which is load-bearing for the quantum-trace uniqueness proof (Theorem 6 / 29), is verified only for M \ensuremath{\in} \{0,1,2,3\}; the general inductive step is asserted without being written down (C9, minor, technical\_correctness).
  \item Two bibliography entries (Mur, WRT) appear in the reference list without explicit in-text citation markers in the provided manuscript sections, weakening their bibliographic justification (citation specialist).
  \item Self-citations [Cr1] and [Cr2] are incorrectly attributed to 'the second author' in the manuscript text, whereas C. Anghel is the first author of both those papers and of the present paper (citation specialist).
\end{itemize}

\section*{Revision Targets}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item [open] paper\_tex at `Theorem 8, restated as Theorem 34`: Add a separate lemma showing that for every generator g \ensuremath{\in} C\_N there exists a braid \ensuremath{\beta} whose normalized closure scalar contains g as a coefficient of v\_0 \ensuremath{\to} v\_0, so vanishing in the target quotient is necessary for Reidemeister II/III invariance. Alternatively, derive the maximality from a universality argument à la Reshetikhin--Turaev for the truncated category. A small computational supplement (e.g. verification/maximality\_check.py) confirming that for N=4 the unknotting move forces every C\_N-generator into the kernel would also help. Check: Re-review should confirm `Theorem 8, restated as Theorem 34` is corrected or justified.
  \item [open] paper\_tex at `Remark 11`: Provide at least one explicit computational example: compute tilde \ensuremath{\Omega}\_4 and tilde \ensuremath{\Omega}\_6 for a small candidate pair of knots (e.g. mutant pairs Kinoshita--Terasaka / Conway, or 11n\_34 / 11n\_42) and show numerically that tilde \ensuremath{\Omega}\_N distinguishes them while every J\_d, \ensuremath{\Phi}\_d at d|N do not. Ship the code as verification/richer\_structure\_example.py using a quantum-trace implementation (e.g. on top of snappy or a custom braid implementation). \section*{Open Questions}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item For every generator g of C\_N, does there exist an explicit braid \ensuremath{\beta} such that the normalized quantum-trace scalar of the closure \ensuremath{\beta}\^{} contains g as a coefficient --- thereby making vanishing of g in the quotient ring a necessary condition for Reidemeister-II/III invariance? If so, which braid witnesses each generator?
  \item Can tilde \ensuremath{\Omega}\_4 or tilde \ensuremath{\Omega}\_6 be computed explicitly for at least one knot pair (e.g., Kinoshita--Terasaka / Conway mutants) and shown to separate them while every J\_d and \ensuremath{\Phi}\_d at d|N agree? If no such pair is currently known, should Remark 11 be recast as a conjecture rather than an assertion?
  \item What is the general M step of the inductive argument for Lemma 31? In particular, what is the closed-form expression for R\_\{v\_\{M,j\}\}\^{}\{v\_\{M,j\}\} \ensuremath{-} R\_\{v\_\{M+1,j\}\}\^{}\{v\_\{M+1,j\}\} that makes the telescoping work for arbitrary M \ensuremath{\le} N \ensuremath{-} 2?
  \item Are the typographic errors in Theorems 29, 37, and 39 purely transcription artifacts, or does any one of them reflect a substantive ambiguity in the ring-theoretic cancellation argument --- specifically, is the generator of the ideal I\_N in Theorem 39 \ensuremath{\phi}\_N(q\^{}2)\ensuremath{\cdot}(s \ensuremath{-} q\^{}\{1\ensuremath{-}N\}) or some other element?
  \item Why are the bibliography entries [Mur] and [WRT] included in the reference list without in-text citation in the main body? Are they cited in sections not extracted for review, or are they listed for background purposes only?
\end{itemize}

This shows that this\textbackslash{}n\$d\$-part of the ideal, generated by both terms\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}varphi\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}(q\^{}2)\$ and \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}frac\{s\^{}\{2d\}-1\}\{s\^{}2-1\}\$ has a rich\textbackslash{}nstructure which in turn suggests that the invariant itself could encode\textbackslash{}ndeeper information than the sequence of coloured Jones and ADO\textbackslash{}ninvariants at levels that divide \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$.\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n2.5ex -1.5ex Further directions 2.5ex -1.5ex Structure of the level\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$ universal invariant We would like to study the form of the\textbackslash{}nmaximal ring at non-prime levels \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}widetilde\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbb L\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\}\$\textbackslash{}nand the information encoded in the maximal level \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$ universal\textbackslash{}ninvariant at\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}widetilde\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Omega\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\}(L)(q,s) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}widetilde\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbb L\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\}\$.\textbackslash{}n2.5ex -1.5ex Geometrical Level \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$ universal invariant In\textbackslash{}n[@Cr2], [@Cr1] the author constructed universal knot invariants and\textbackslash{}nunifications of coloured Jones and ADO polynomials using topological\textbackslash{}ntools, based on configuration spaces in the punctured disc. The level\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$ universal and level \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$ unified invariant should\textbackslash{}nhave purely topological counterparts in that context, given by\textbackslash{}nLagrangian intersections in configuration spaces. We are planning to\textbackslash{}ninvestigate such models for our future research. 2.5ex -1.5ex Level\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$ universal invariants for \$3\$-manifolds This direction\textbackslash{}nconcerns the lift of the level \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathcal\{N\}\$ universal knot invariants\textbackslash{}nto invariants for \$3\$-manifolds. Coloured Jones and ADO knot invariants\textbackslash{}nare building blocks for the Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants\textbackslash{}n([@Witt], [@RT]) and the Costantino-Geer-Patureau invariant ([@BCGP])\textbackslash{}nrespectively.       "statement": "If the level N is a prime natural number, then the ring Li\_N is the largest quotient of the polynomial ring Li with the property that the image of the quantum trace in this quotient gives a knot invariant. \subsection*{summary (\texttt{claude-haiku-4-5-20251001})}
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\{\\
  "audience": "Knot theorists and quantum topology researchers; mathematicians working with quantum groups, braid group representations, and knot invariants; researchers interested in unifying different families of quantum invariants and exploring connections to 3-manifold topology.",\\
  "key\_contributions": [\\
    "Construction of level N unified invariants for any level N \ensuremath{\ge} 2, represented in maximal quotient rings of the polynomial ring Q[q\^{}\ensuremath{\pm}2, s\^{}\ensuremath{\pm}2]",\\
    "Proof that for prime N, the interpolation ring gives the maximal quotient allowing knot invariants from the N-part of the Verma module",\\
    "Explicit interpolation formula showing the unified invariant equals a combination of coloured Jones and ADO invariants",\\
    "Extension to non-prime N with a richer maximal ring structure that recovers both classical invariants but potentially contains additional information",\\
    "Demonstration that the universal invariants specialize to both semi-simple (Jones) and non-semisimple (ADO) invariants through coefficient specialization"\\
  ],\\
  "plain\_language\_summary": "Quantum knot invariants are algebraic tools that help distinguish knots by assigning polynomial or other algebraic objects to them. The coloured Jones polynomials and ADO (Akutsu-Deguchi-Ohtsuki) invariants are two fundamental families of such invariants derived from quantum group representation theory, each revealing different geometric information about knots. This paper constructs new \textbackslash{}"level N universal invariants\textbackslash{}" that unify both families by leveraging the Verma module---an infinite-dimensional representation of the quantum group U\_q(sl\_2)---and examining how it acts on braids when restricted to finite-dimensional subspaces.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThe authors work over polynomial rings in two variables and define a maximal quotient ring structure for each level N. For prime levels, this quotient ring is relatively simple and captures an interpolation formula between coloured Jones and ADO invariants. For non-prime levels, the quotient ring has richer structure with potentially new information not visible in the classical sequences of invariants. The paper proves that their invariants are maximal---no larger quotient ring can produce well-defined knot invariants from the Verma module at that level.",\\
  "tldr": "A construction of universal quantum knot invariants that unify and extend the coloured Jones and ADO polynomials through quantum traces on quotients of the Verma module."\\
\}\\
\end{quote}
